description: Create a schedule build for a DataModel.

build_type.description: Type of the build, one of ``"ACCUMULATE"``, ``"FULL"``, or ``"SCHEMA_CHANGES"``. Defaults to ``"ACCUMULATE"``.

days.description: Keyword-only. List of days for a cron schedule, e.g. ``["SUN", "MON", "TUE", "WED", "THU", "FRI", "SAT"]`` or ``["*"]`` for all days.

hour.description: Keyword-only. Hour in 24-hour format (UTC) for a cron schedule.

minute.description: Keyword-only. Minute of the hour (UTC) for a cron schedule.

interval_days.description: Keyword-only. Interval in days for an interval-based schedule.

interval_hours.description: Keyword-only. Interval in hours for an interval-based schedule.

interval_minutes.description: Keyword-only. Interval in minutes for an interval-based schedule.

examples.user_query: Schedule a full build for the 'SalesDataModel' data model every Monday at 3:00 UTC.
examples.notes: This call schedules a full build of the 'SalesDataModel' to run every Monday at 3:00 AM UTC using a cron-based schedule.

examples.user_query: I need to set up an interval-based build for 'MarketingAnalytics' to run every 2 days and 6 hours. How can I do that?
examples.notes: This call creates an interval-based schedule for the 'MarketingAnalytics' DataModel to build every 2 days and 6 hours. The build type defaults to 'ACCUMULATE'.

examples.user_query: Can I create a schema changes build for 'FinanceModel' to run daily at 12:30 UTC?
examples.notes: This call schedules a schema changes build for the 'FinanceModel' to run daily at 12:30 PM UTC using a cron-based schedule.

description: Retrieve all dashboard shares, including user and group details for each shared dashboard.

examples.user_query: Show me all the dashboards and who they are shared with.
examples.notes: This retrieves a list of all dashboards along with details of the users and groups they are shared with. Useful for auditing dashboard sharing settings.

examples.user_query: I need to see which groups have access to our dashboards.
examples.notes: This call fetches all dashboards and includes group sharing details, making it helpful for understanding group-level access.

examples.user_query: Can I get a list of all users who have access to our dashboards?
examples.notes: This retrieves all dashboards and their associated user sharing details, which is useful for reviewing individual user access.

description: Fetch all users and groups and build ID-to-name lookup maps.

examples.user_query: Fetch all user emails and group names to resolve share entries.
examples.notes: This call retrieves mappings of user IDs to emails and group IDs to names, useful for resolving share entries in dashboards or data models.

examples.user_query: How can I get a mapping of user IDs to emails and group IDs to names?
examples.notes: Use this to fetch user and group lookup maps for resolving IDs into readable names or emails in shared resources.

examples.user_query: Retrieve user and group mappings to identify shared dashboard entries.
examples.notes: This example demonstrates how to obtain user and group ID-to-name mappings to help identify shared entries in dashboards or data models.
